scope: Reconcile current ACadSharp repeated-record, EED-size and nested-block-copy issue leads; ODA EED/BS contracts; LibreDWG 0.14.1 safety changes; and local libdxfrw source/test coverage, then refine 7K implementation readiness without expanding the routine validation loop.

method.kind: Read-only web research and local source/test inventory audit
method.evidenceRule: Peer issue titles/reports are route-specific discovery leads, not format rules or evidence of matching local defects. ODA v5.4.1 controls DWG byte-layout conclusions. Local writer/reader symmetry and generated self-readback can prove local wire behavior only, not independent or native acceptance.

observed: The detailed report describes recursion per comment, XDATA APPID block, and IMAGE/WIPEOUT clip-boundary group 91, with process-crash claims at peer-specific thresholds.
The local plan already records generated 20,000-record comment, XDATA, and WIPEOUT controls in the hardening owner and a passing focused CTest receipt.
The local regression does not assert a format maximum or peer equivalence.
doesNotEstablish: That peer crash thresholds are suitable local resource caps
evidence.planUse: Keep the existing repeated-record slice closed and avoid repeating it or adding per-slice crash/fuzz work.

evidence.topic: ACadSharp #1282 EED size and ODA application-length contract
observed: The current ACadSharp issue index title says the DWG writer loses an object when extended data exceeds 32,767 bytes per application; the issue body was not retrieved.
ODA v5.4.1 §28 defines per-application EED length as BS, excluding its own prefix and the application handle; §2.2 describes BS as a 16-bit encoding.
Local encodeDwgEed uses uint16_t and flushes before app data would exceed UINT16_MAX; the local decoder uses unsigned BS sizes and bounds chunks.
The test inventory includes reader-side EED boundary vectors but no direct DWG-writer test at 32,767/32,768 or 65,535/65,536.
doesNotEstablish: That repeated chunks with the same APPID are accepted by an independent producer/native application
evidence.planUse: Add generated local writer boundary tests around the reported signed threshold and unsigned 16-bit boundary; keep continuation semantics LOCAL_WIRE_ONLY until externally accepted. Do not change limits from the issue title.

evidence.topic: DXF XDATA group-1004 physical chunk boundary
observed: The local XDATA writer splits group-1004 hex payloads into chunks of at most 127 bytes, and the binary DXF writer rejects a single group-1004 value above that size.
Existing 127-byte application-group tests in wave1_tests exercise group 310, not group 1004.
No explicit local 1004 126/127/128 writer boundary test was found.
doesNotEstablish: A production defect in the current splitter
That group-310 test coverage proves the group-1004 code path
evidence.planUse: Add small ASCII/Binary controls under the current XDATA writer selector; inspect emitted groups and following-record alignment.

evidence.topic: ACadSharp #1283 nested block copying and LibreDWG safety cross-check
observed: ACadSharp's live issue index title reports quadratic nested-block copying and stack exhaustion; its issue body was not retrieved.
Local DRW_Insert stores a block name/reference and core blocks are represented as separate records; no equivalent recursive block-deep-copy API was identified.

LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS lists independent capacity/logical-size, checked arithmetic, progress, stale-pointer, and loss fixes, reinforcing that byte limits, traversal work, depth, and identity are distinct safety concerns.
doesNotEstablish: A common root cause between ACadSharp and LibreDWG reports
A reason to add broad performance or sanitizer work to the fast loop
evidence.planUse: Keep #1283 as a discovery prompt under current graph/work-budget owners. Any future flatten/copy path gets a bounded work/identity test at its owner; optional peer/fuzz evidence stays at the composed checkpoint.
